summary.short: Chinese CAC rules, in force from promulgation, that set when data processors must pass a national security assessment, sign a standard contract or obtain certification before providing data abroad, and exempt listed low-risk transfers from those steps.
summary.long: Order No. 16 of the Cyberspace Administration of China, adopted at the CAC's 2023 26th office meeting and in force from its publication. It governs outbound provision of data by data processors. Exemptions (Arts. 2-6) cover data that is neither personal information nor important data, transfers in international trade, cross-border transport and academic cooperation, foreign-collected data processed in China, transfers needed for contracts with individuals, cross-border HR management and emergencies, and transfers by non-CIIO processors of personal information of fewer than 100,000 people (excluding sensitive data) cumulatively since 1 January. A security assessment through the provincial CAC is required for CIIO operators transferring personal information or important data, and for other processors transferring important data or personal information of 1 million or more people, or sensitive personal information of 10,000 or more (Art. 7). Non-CIIO processors transferring data of 100,000 to under 1 million people, or under 10,000 sensitive-data subjects, must sign a standard contract or obtain personal information protection certification (Art. 8). Assessment results are valid for three years, extendable by three years on application (Art. 9). Processors must also meet consent, notice and impact assessment duties (Art. 10), data security and incident reporting duties (Art. 11), and local CAC supervision (Art. 12). Free trade zones may set negative lists subject to provincial approval and filing (Art. 6). The rules prevail over conflicting 2022 and 2023 measures (Art. 13).

obligations.summary: Data processors exporting data must apply through the local provincial CAC to the national CAC for a data export security assessment in the listed cases: CII operators exporting personal information or important data; other processors exporting important data, or cumulatively exporting personal information of 1 million or more persons or sensitive personal information of 10,000 or more persons since 1 January.
obligations.applies_from: from promulgation (自公布之日起施行, Art. 14)
obligations.conditional_on: cases listed in Art. 7 items (1) and (2); exemptions in Arts. 3 to 6 prevail

obligations.summary: Processors other than CII operators that cumulatively export personal information of 100,000 to under 1 million persons, or sensitive personal information of under 10,000 persons, must conclude a personal information export standard contract with the overseas recipient or pass personal information protection certification.
obligations.applies_from: from promulgation (自公布之日起施行, Art. 14)

obligations.summary: An approved security assessment result is valid for 3 years from issuance. Processors may apply through the provincial CAC to extend validity, filing up to 60 working days before expiry if activities continue and no reassessment-triggering change has occurred; the national CAC may extend by 3 years.

obligations.conditional_on: continued export activities and no change requiring a new security assessment
